title: Anagram Groups
statement:
A word list is given as one string, `words`, with the words separated by single spaces. Put two words in the same **group** if one is an anagram of the other (the same letters in a different order, or the same word twice).

Return the **number of groups**.
constraints: each word has 1 to 20 lowercase letters
words are separated by exactly one space (no leading or trailing space)

args: eat tea tan ate nat bat

hints.nudge: Two words are in the same group exactly when they share some 'signature'. What could that signature be?
hints.pattern: Use a hash set of canonical keys: the word's letters sorted.
hints.walkthrough: Comparing every pair of words is O(n^2) comparisons. Instead give each word a key that is identical for all its anagrams: sort its letters (eat, tea and ate all become aet). Put all keys in a set; the number of different keys is the number of groups. Sorting a word of length L costs O(L log L), so the whole thing is O(n * L log L).
